answer: The pearl multiplier is published, charged in walnut, and relic lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4660 identities would post 2786 proofs and burn roughly 49 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
